text:
alex: Anyone else seeing timeouts from our GPU node pool to model-cache service via the VPCE in ap-southeast-2? Started ~5m ago, pods hitting TLS timeout to model-cache.internal.vpce.amazonaws.com:443
maria: yep, saw curl hang from a training job, same VPC/subnet. No obvious errors from kube-proxy. :thinking_face:
sre-bot: ALERT: vpce-0abc1234 connectivity degraded (eni-subnet-03) — 9 instances affected — created 1733024100
kevin: first suspects: security group on the interface endpoint or DNS resolving to public IPs (Private DNS disabled). Can someone run a quick dig + describe-vpc-endpoints?
jess: ran quick checks, posting snippets:
```
$ dig +short model-cache.us-east-1.vpce.amazonaws.com
54.239.34.12
```
and
```
$ aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --vpc-endpoint-ids vpce-0abc1234 --query 'VpcEndpoints[0].PrivateDnsEnabled'
false
```
That looks like it's resolving to the public IP because PrivateDnsEnabled is false. Nodes in these subnets don't have NAT at the moment (we spun down a NAT in AZ-b earlier).
maria: ah, during the NAT maintenance we forgot to restore the route for those subnets, so no egress to internet. If DNS returns public IPs they can't reach service. PrivateLink would avoid that if private DNS was enabled.
kevin: yep. Two parallel fixes: re-enable NAT route (fast), or enable Private DNS on the vpce so the service name resolves to the endpoint ENI private IPs. Also double-check endpoint SG allows inbound 443 from our node CIDR.
alex: checking SG now. Running: 
```
$ aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters Name=attachment.instance-owner-id,Values=vpce
```
Found ENIs in subnets a/b/c. SG on the ENI was only allowing 10.20.0.0/16, but our GPU nodes are in 10.21.0.0/16 (we split ranges last quarter).
jess: that SG mismatch would definitely block traffic even if DNS resolved to private IPs. We should add the node CIDR temporarily.
kevin: proposed steps (quick):
1) add 10.21.0.0/16 to vpce SG inbound 443
2) enable Private DNS on vpce: `aws ec2 modify-vpc-endpoint --vpc-endpoint-id vpce-0abc1234 --private-dns-enabled`
3) if still blocked, re-add NAT route for the subnet to restore egress until DNS flips.
alex: applied SG change and enabled private DNS. Also flushed pod DNS cache by restarting a failing pod.
(about 60s later)
alex: quick test: `curl -v https://model-cache.us-east-1.vpce.amazonaws.com/health` -> HTTP/1.1 200 OK :tada:
maria: nice. Any follow-up to avoid re-occurence?
kevin: playbook items:
- Ensure private-dns-enabled is part of our vpce terraform module default true (we had manual creation for this vpce).
- Add terraform check for vpce SG to include all node CIDRs.
- Add a small runbook for NAT maintenance reminding to validate PrivateLink DNS behavior.
jess: filing infra ticket to migrate this vpce to infra-managed module and add unit test for PrivateDnsEnabled=true.
sre-bot: RESOLVED: vpce-0abc1234 recovered. Alert cleared at 1733024278
alex: root cause summary: Private DNS was disabled on the interface endpoint, so clients resolved the public IP and relied on NAT egress which was down in the affected AZ + security group on the ENI lacked the GPU node CIDR. Fixed by enabling private DNS + updating SG.
maria: great postmortem, tagging infra-runbooks and scheduling a retro. :white_check_mark:
